title: hnA TacFPS Aim Guide
author: trgjtk
scope: TacFPS practice for Valorant and other low-time-to-kill games. Aim training develops the mouse-control component and must be paired with in-game deathmatch or an equivalent transfer activity.
concepts: Transfer depends on practising the mouse movement the game demands, not merely raising an aim-trainer score.
A flick combines the path toward the target with the ability to decelerate and stop on it. Fast TacFPS acquisition puts unusual emphasis on stopping power.
Misses tend to extend along the direction of travel: at higher speed, overshoot and undershoot grow more than sideways path error.
Large static targets permit speed without enough precision; tiny static targets often reward accuracy at a slower speed. Training should deliberately cover both ends and the transition between them.
Horizontal and vertical acquisition impose different joint and lever demands, so both need exposure rather than assuming one transfers perfectly to the other.
practice_rules: Follow the execution goal for the current routine; the same scenario produces a different adaptation when played for raw speed versus clean pathing.
Pair the routines with game-specific deathmatch so mouse control is integrated with movement, crosshair placement, target recognition, and decisions.
Rotate the three routines one per day. Use Speed and Stopping more often when fast acquisition is the main limitation; use Smooth Pathing more often when lines and corrections are uncontrolled.
Treat discomfort as a stop signal. Productive speed work may involve brief controlled tension, but pain and sustained gripping are not training goals.
rotation: Default cycle: Speed and Stopping, Speed-to-Precision, Smooth Pathing. When uncertain, repeat that three-day cycle. A speed-biased cycle can repeat the first routine before continuing to the second and third.

routines.name: TacFPS - Speed and Stopping
routines.description: Raw acquisition speed and controlled deceleration. Hold Mouse1 continuously, snap aggressively, and reacquire immediately after a miss rather than polishing the path.
routines.sensitivity: Use normal in-game sensitivity; the source assumes roughly 35-70 cm/360.
author_guidance: Hold Mouse1 continuously for every scenario in this routine.
Snap onto each target as fast as physically possible; large misses are acceptable while training this speed.
Reacquire immediately after a miss. Both the initial flick and the correction should be fast, and the correction does not need to be one clean movement.
Do not optimize for smoothness in this routine. The intended adaptation is raw acquisition speed and stopping power.
Use the target-switching and static exercises together to practise rapid acquisition across different movement sizes and directions.

exercises.focus: Use horizontal short, medium, and long switches to practise rapid stops.
Accelerate and stop over the smaller movements common after sound crosshair placement.
Keep the same aggressive acquisition while handling more vertical displacement.
Snap quickly, then stabilize on the small target.

exercises.scenario: Pokeball Frenzy Auto Wide Wall 3 Targets
exercises.focus: Apply fast stops across wider target spacing.
Combine a forceful initial movement with precise stabilization.
Reacquire the blinking target immediately, like correcting onto an unexpected swing.

routines.name: TacFPS - Speed-to-Precision
routines.description: Bridge raw speed into consistent static acquisition. Perform the speed runs first, then retain the initial pace while cleaning up the final correction during accuracy runs.
routines.sensitivity: The source recommends roughly 25-35 cm/360 for this block.
author_guidance: Use this routine to carry the speed from Routine 1 into more consistent and precise acquisition.
In fuglaaPressure, attempt every target before it disappears; missing matters less than making every attempt.
For the three static scenarios, always complete the prescribed speed runs before the accuracy runs.
During speed runs, increase shots fired while keeping accuracy between 60% and 80%.
During accuracy runs, target 90-95% accuracy while retaining the fast initial flick and making the final micro-correction disciplined.
For the reflex scenarios, use one motion to the target and one back to center; adjust time scale or difficulty using the stated accuracy thresholds.

exercises.focus: Attempt every target before it disappears. Use the four-target version when accuracy remains below 60%.
Do 7 speed runs at 60-80% accuracy, then 3 disciplined accuracy runs at 90-95%.
Do 5 speed runs at 60-80% accuracy, then 2 accuracy runs at 90-95%.
Do 3 speed runs at 60-80% accuracy, then 2 accuracy runs at 90-95%.
Use one movement out and back. Increase time scale above 50% accuracy; reduce it below 25%.
Use one decisive movement to the target and one back to center; switch to an easier version below 25% accuracy.

routines.name: TacFPS - Smooth Pathing
routines.description: Train the opposite end of the spectrum: direct lines, minimal correction, and clean stops. Slow down enough to make the path deliberate rather than chasing score.
routines.sensitivity: The source recommends roughly 20-25 cm/360 for this block.
author_guidance: This routine deliberately trains the smoothness and pathing end of the spectrum rather than raw speed.
For the static and pokeball exercises, use the straightest possible path, minimize micro-corrections, and stop cleanly on target.
Move slowly enough to preserve that efficient path; score and maximum pace are not the objective here.
For the two tracking exercises, follow the slow target precisely without shaking off it.
Use the tracking work to clean up flick paths and final micro-adjustments.

exercises.focus: Draw straight paths and stop cleanly with as few micro-corrections as possible.
Prioritize line efficiency and deliberate stops over pace.
Keep long movements straight and settle without extra correction.
Maintain a clean line into stable contact on each target.
Track the slow target without visible shake to clean up pathing and final corrections.
Use precise smooth pursuit without introducing corrective jitter.
